Secondary_Symptoms: No changes in urine color or frequency

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with recent onset of edema and significant proteinuria.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—let’s start with key questions. How old are you, and when did the edema and the proteinuria begin? Patient: Now please continue your dialogue Doctor: Are you having foamy urine, visible blood in urine, reduced urination, or high blood pressure?

Patient: I’m 25, and the swelling started over the past several days, mainly around my eyes and ankles. I haven’t noticed foamy urine, visible blood, or reduced urination, and I’m not aware of any high blood pressure.

Doctor: Any recent fever/infection, sore throat, or skin/scalp rash before the swelling, and are you taking NSAIDs (ibuprofen/naproxen), new antibiotics, or other new meds? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with urine protein quantification (UPCR or 24h protein) and urine microscopy (RBC casts, dysmorphic RBCs).

RESULTS: Temperature 36.8°C; Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg; Heart Rate 82 bpm; Respiratory Rate 14/min. Mild periorbital and ankle edema. Cardiovascular: Normal S1/S2, no murmurs. Respiratory: Clear bilaterally. Abdomen: No distension; normal bowel sounds; soft, non-tender, no organomegaly. Neuro: No focal deficits. Labs: Serum Na 140 mmol/L; K 3.5 mmol/L; Albumin 1.9 g/dL; Total bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL; Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL. Urinalysis: Proteinuria 4+; Fatty casts present. (Urine microscopy details requested for RBC casts/dysmorphic RBCs and urine protein quantification [UPCR/24h] not provided in the available data—UNAVAILABLE.)

Doctor: I’ve reviewed your data—at age 25 with rapid onset edema and severe proteinuria (4+), hypoalbuminemia (albumin 1.9), and fatty casts. Are you having any recent sore throat/skin infection (2–6 weeks) or have you noticed cola-colored urine or flank pain? Patient: Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Urine protein quantification (UPCR or 24h), plus repeat urine microscopy specifically for RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs; also REQUEST TEST: ANA, C3/C4, hepatitis B/C, HIV; and consider REQUEST TEST: serum free light chains. Patient: Doctor: If the microscopy shows nephrotic syndrome without hematuria (no RBC casts/dysmorphic RBCs) and complement is normal, this most strongly fits minimal change disease (often steroid-responsive). DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic syndrome—most consistent with Minimal Change Disease (pending confirmation with urine microscopy for absence of RBC casts and normal complement).
